findings.problem: Employer social security (US-005) is 195.98 = 6.2% x 3,161 with no wage-base cap. The employee line on the same payslip is capped at 186.00 (H72) because only 3,000 of wage base remains (184,500 - 181,500). The employer share is also limited to the 184,500 base, so the employer block overstates the tax by 9.98. The same typed value sits in United States (ES)!H36 and Compliance Payslip!H36, and the totals in H38 (241.81) are wrong too. Source: generator 06-payslip/_build/build_psl.py line 123, d['er_ss'] = fica_wages x employer rate, with no cap.
findings.expected: H36 = 186.00 as a formula, the lesser of (employer rate x wage base - employer tax already paid) and ROUND(H67 x employer rate,2), mirroring H69:H72 (or =H72 where both rates are 6.2%). H38 then = 231.83. Fix it in build_psl.py:123 and rebuild all three tabs.
findings.evidence: Live WebFetch 2026-11-04 of https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i941.pdf (Rev. March 2026): 'The social security tax rate is 6.2% each for the employee and employer. The social security wage base limit is $184,500.' Cached values: H72=186.00, H36=195.98.

findings.problem: The Medicare YTD wages are =H68+H67, where H68 is 'Social security wages paid before this payslip'. Social security wages stop at the 184,500 base, so H77 can never pass the 200,000 Additional Medicare threshold. The Additional Medicare line (H78:H79, US-008) therefore always computes 0, whatever the employee earned. H61 (YTD Medicare) uses the same H77 and leaves out Additional Medicare. The sample only gives the right answer because it sits below both limits. The same applies on the ES and Compliance Payslip tabs.
findings.expected: Add an input row 'Medicare wages paid before this payslip (year to date)' (uncapped) and use it in H77 and H61. YTD Medicare withheld = prior YTD Medicare tax + H74 + H79. Keep H68 for social security only.

findings.problem: Employer Medicare 45.83 (H37) and YTD Gross 185,000 (H58) are typed values on rows that should be calculated. The toolkit validate_workbook --artifact PSL --totals-check flags H58 under C26. YTD gross 185,000 also does not reconcile with the YTD social security wages (181,500 before + 3,161 this period = 184,661) plus the cafeteria-plan deductions. The same applies on the ES and Compliance Payslip tabs.
findings.expected: H37 =ROUND(H67*employer Medicare rate,2). H58 = an input 'YTD gross before this payslip' + H22, chosen so that YTD gross >= YTD social security wages + YTD section-125 deductions.

findings.problem: The workbook has no 'Total Hours Worked' field. CA Lab. Code 226(a)(2) requires total hours worked (fact psl.ca.statement.content: 'total hours (not for salaried exempt)'). HI 387-6(c) ('total hours'), CT, IA, IN, MA, MI, NE, NM, PA, RI, VT, WA and WI facts ask for hours worked. The payslip prints hours per line only (G19=80, G20=4) and never the total (84). _research/PSL-legal-items.json item 'hours' (label 'Total hours worked') is matched to 'Regular Hours', so C57 passes on the wrong field.
findings.expected: Add a payslip row 'Total hours worked' = sum of the hours of the time-based lines (accumulator US-030) under the earnings block on all three tabs. Add a Payslip Spec row with HRP mapping $payroll.hours.total and the naming States. Change PSL-legal-items 'hours'.match to ['Total Hours Worked'].

The Spec has rows for Tips (B42), Allowances (B40) and Piece-rate (B39) only.
findings.expected: Add 6 Payslip Spec rows (Field Name EN/ES, HRP mapping, 2-4 sentence explanation), each with its DD field (bank account fields) or 'payroll result, no DD field' and the naming States (DC, CT, MI). Account masking rule: last 4 digits.

findings.problem: The paid leave block has accrued, used and available hours only. AZ requires 'the amount of pay received as earned paid sick time' (fact psl.az.sick_leave.on_statement, register US-AZS5-011 subsection C). NYC requires PTO accrued in the period, paid and unpaid PTO used in the period, and unpaid immediately available hours (fact psl.nyc.pto.on_statement, US-NYB5-003). Neither the payslip nor the Spec (B30:B32) can show these, so the AZ and NYC rows of LEAVE_BALANCE_RULE cannot be met.
findings.expected: Add switched rows: 'Paid sick leave pay received year to date (USD)' (AZ), plus 'PTO accrued this period', 'Paid PTO used this period', 'Unpaid PTO used this period' and 'Unpaid PTO available' (NYC). Add the matching Spec rows naming AZ and NYC.

findings.problem: The SSN mapping CONCAT('***-**-';SUBSTRING($person.ssn;6;4)) prints the last 4 digits for every State. Maryland bars any SSN, even truncated, on the wage check and attachments (psl.md.ssn.rule, US-MDS5-008), but the bar appears only as prose in E25. A developer following column D would breach LE 3-502(d).
findings.expected: D25 = IF($employment.work_state='MD';'';CONCAT('***-**-';SUBSTRING($person.ssn;6;4))), with Employee ID as the identifier in MD. E25 should say which States print nothing. The SUBSTRING positions are correct: the DD SSN is N(9).

numeric_verification.method: Independent QA F44 (auditor script, no builder code imported) over all 160 distinct [[FACT:key=value]] tags (193 tag occurrences) of the workbook. Each value equals a fact entry effective in 2026, across all _research/*-facts.json files. Each printed register id is one of the fact's register ids. Each register row exists, is tier A.x, active, and verified within 120 days. Every numeric, section and date element of the value was found in the row's local copy (PDF via PyMuPDF, HTML/gzip/txt stripped); 160/160 OK. Live WebFetch 2026-11-04: IRS i941 Rev. 3-2026 confirms 184,500 / 6.2% each side / 1.45% / 0.9% / 200,000. IRS p15t (2026) confirms Worksheet 1A line 1g 8,600/12,900, the STANDARD Single/MFS thresholds 0/7,500/19,900/57,900/113,200/209,275/263,725/648,100 and the 0-37% rates. That is 9/9 payslip-tab federal tags live. SSA cbb.html and leginfo CA 226 returned HTTP 403, so the local copies were used. facts_total = 160 tagged + 17 PSL facts not placed because the builder could not prove their wording in the saved copy (the 17 f44 gaps PSL-RQ-01,04,05,06,09,10,12,13,14,16,17,18,19,20,21,25,27; known item, the source hunter is working on them). The 11 'open' requests are unresolved research, not facts.

_judgments.C49_KW-100: Not a PSL defect. KW-100 is the Kansas Department of Revenue withholding guide id (register US-KSS5-001 / US-KSP51-003, https://www.ksrevenue.gov/kw100.html) cited in CCG table 206 r11c2. It matches the C49 code pattern by coincidence; no WTC code is involved. The exemption validation_exemptions.C49 has a reason, source URL and decided_on, so it is valid per contract 1.4.0. Its owner row US-OWN-011 is missing from the register (PSL-QA1-21). content_checks.py honours exemptions only for missing inputs, so C49 stays printed as FAIL; that is a shared-tool limitation, carried as in earlier reviews.
_judgments.C46: Checker false positives, not PSL defects. (a) 4 mismatches, at Compliance Payslip!A65, EN!A65, ES!A65 and Payslip Spec!E50: the tag says 184,500 and the checker compares it with the last dated entry, 192,300 (US-FEDB5-401, effective 2027-01-01). The fact effective 2026-01-01..2026-12-31 is 184,500 (US-FEDS5-005) and the sample pay date is 10/23/2026, so the tag is correct (live i941 Rev. 3-2026 confirms). (b) 8 unbound, at Field Option B/D 195, 317, 339 and 348: these are the wage-type identifiers 21100, US-175, US-214 and US-225, whose digits collide with ia.sui.wage_base 21100 (the 2027 value), al.wh...reduction_per_step / ut oracle 175, oh.pit.school_district.count 214 and nv...registration_threshold 225. They are not fact values. Same residue class as SIR-QA1-19 (shared C46 is neither period-aware nor identifier-aware). Owner of shared/ fixes the checker, or the owner records validation_exemptions.C46. The auditor does not write exemptions. Not counted as a PSL finding.
_judgments.Spec_42_rows: Accepted. 25-35 is a target, the minimum of 20 is met, and the union of 51 State element lists plus the federal lines needs more. Round 2 adds rows (PSL-QA1-04, 05, 06, 09, 10), so the count will grow; that is expected, not a defect.
_judgments.pay_line_code_form: Accepted. Real WTC codes ('62100 - Basic salary') instead of 'XXXXX - ...' are traceable: each code and name equals US-WTC-001 v1.0, and the form is C29-clean (an X-run next to a dash trips C29). How to set up Payslip!C13 and Payslip Spec D41/D47 document the code-dash-name form.
_judgments.SS_cap_logic_2026: The employee side is correct for 2026: wage base 184,500 (fact US-FEDS5-005, effective 2026), lesser-of rule, not annualised-then-divided, 186.00. The employer side does not apply the cap (PSL-QA1-01, blocker). The Medicare YTD basis cannot trigger the Additional Medicare tax (PSL-QA1-02).
